title: Flows are blind to licence gates - no licence in the Flow drawer, and a refused gate is a silent no-op
description: MpiFlowLibrary has no licence awareness at all: no "Licence required" chip on the tile, no licence row in its detail drawer, no read-the-licence / request-authorization / report-misuse links. The Model Library has all three. Consent is NOT bypassed - downloadService.start() is the chokepoint and fires for a flow key too - so this is an ambush plus a dead end: a refused gate returns undefined, creating no job and emitting no download:started, so the flow tile silently reverts to Install with no explanation. Live today on scribble, scribble-object and object-stamp, which all require klein-9b, the app's only verify licence (HF token + a grant taken on Black Forest Labs' own page). MPI-591 sharpens it by putting territory-gated MiniMax H3 behind Extend Video, where the "Request authorization" link a barred user needs exists only in the gate dialog and the Model Library drawer. Found while closing MPI-664, whose attribution decision rests on the same fact: a Flow user may never open the Model Library.
